Graduate unemployment and the jobs that follow

Does longer unemployment predict next-month entry into an occupation that typically requires less than a bachelor’s degree?

Monthly CPS, 2011–2025 · Linked transitions and adjusted models

Below-BA entry risk falls with elapsed unemployment in both birth groups. Observed transitions do not identify changes in willingness to accept a lower-match job.

Micro Econ

Budget constraint

At prices p₁ and p₂, income m limits the affordable combinations of two goods.

p₁x₁ + p₂x₂ ≤ m

A price change changes the budget line’s slope. An income change moves it in parallel when prices stay fixed.

Substitution and income effects

A price change alters relative prices and purchasing power. The substitution effect isolates the response to relative prices under a compensation rule. The income effect captures the remaining change in demand. Hicks compensation holds utility fixed; Slutsky compensation keeps the original bundle affordable.

Revealed preference

If a consumer chooses bundle A when bundle B is also affordable, A is directly revealed preferred to B. Revealed-preference conditions test whether observed choices are consistent with utility maximization.

Macro Econ

Nominal and real balances

Nominal balances measure money in currency units. Real balances measure its purchasing power relative to a price level P.

Real balances = M / P
Money and expenditureMV = PY

With velocity defined as nominal expenditure divided by the money stock, this is an identity. It becomes a theory of prices only with additional assumptions about velocity, output, and the determination of money.

Precautionary money demand

Uncertain receipts and payments create a reason to hold a liquid buffer. Desired balances depend on the cost of a shortfall, access to other liquidity, and the opportunity cost of holding money.

Related research questions

Econometrics

Association and causation

A relationship in observed data can reflect selection, confounding, or reverse causality. Regression adjustment supports a causal interpretation only under suitable identification assumptions.

Example: unemployment duration

Interactions and uncertainty

An interaction estimates how a relationship differs across groups or conditions. A nonsignificant interaction does not prove identical relationships.

Notes and example

Risk and conditional shares

Entry risk uses all eligible linked jobseekers as its denominator. A share among reemployed workers conditions on finding a job. The two measures answer different questions.
